neet_che_u15_t02_1.working: In staggered ethane, each C-H on the front carbon lies midway between two rear C-H bonds, so the nearest dihedral angle is 60°.

neet_che_u15_t02_2.working: In a Newman projection the front carbon is a point. The rear carbon is a circle, with its bonds drawn from the circle's edge.

neet_che_u15_t02_3.working: Staggered and eclipsed forms alternate every 60° of rotation, so the minimum rotation is 60°.

neet_che_u15_t02_4.working: The rotational barrier is only about 12.5 kJ/mol, so the conformers interconvert rapidly at room temperature and cannot be separated; A is false. Staggered ethane does have less torsional strain than eclipsed; R is true.

neet_che_u15_t02_5.working: Per NCERT, bond lengths and bond angles are the same in both conformations, so I is incorrect. In a Sawhorse projection the front carbon is at the lower-left end and the rear carbon at the upper-right, so II is incorrect.
